## If you read on

How it runs

- Students did exercises 1 to 3 at home. Open the [complete notebook](https://ml4ds.com/seminar-teachers/notebook1_complete.html) on screen: blue boxes are hints, opened in order after the room has had a few minutes; green boxes are answers.
- Show the solution of exercise 2 or 3 only if asked. Exercise 2's is the lecture's proof.
- There is no `set.seed`: every student has a different split, on purpose.

What students should see

- Baseline test MSE usually 115 to 190; the line 35 to 75; 5 nearest neighbors 35 to 85.
- Training MSE at `k = 1` exactly zero.
- The winning `k` is 5, 10 or 25 on most splits, and `k = 1` almost never.
- The standard error for 5 nearest neighbors usually 10 to 25.

Where they get stuck

- `order` gives positions, `sort` gives values.
- Looking up neighbors in `test` instead of `train` inside `knn_mse`.
- Reading the standard error as the spread of the losses; it is the spread of their average.
- Leaving `#| eval: false` on a chunk after filling the blank, then wondering why Render shows no output.
- "Why is the training error zero" and "which k is best" are the questions to wait longest on.
